legend: You are an intern at a hyperscale AI data center that manages a linear array of n$$$n$$$ GPUs. The i$$$i$$$-th GPU currently runs a compute load of ai$$$a_i$$$.

The data center hosts workloads for m$$$m$$$ different companies. Each company j$$$j$$$ uses a contiguous range of GPUs from index Lj$$$L_j$$$ to Rj$$$R_j$$$. Different companies may share some GPUs if their computations are colocated for efficiency, so these ranges can overlap.

Before a major demonstration, the management team sets strict balance requirements. For each company j$$$j$$$, the total effective compute load across its range must lie between Aj$$$A_j$$$ and Bj$$$B_j$$$ inclusive.

You are allowed to adjust the load of each GPU by applying an integer change Δi$$$\Delta_i$$$. Each adjustment can either increase or decrease the load, but all must stay within a non-negative common safety limit k$$$k$$$, meaning every GPU's load can change by at most k$$$k$$$ units. The smaller the limit, the better the system stability, so you aim to meet all company requirements using the smallest possible k$$$k$$$.
Additionally, for hardware stability, each GPU must remain above the minimal safe operating load after adjustment: ai+Δi≥1$$$a_i + \Delta_i \ge 1$$$ for all i$$$i$$$.
Find the minimum integer k$$$k$$$ such that there exist integer adjustments Δ1,Δ2,…,Δn$$$\Delta_1, \Delta_2, \ldots, \Delta_n$$$ satisfying, for every company j$$$j$$$,
If this is impossible for any k$$$k$$$, output -1.
input: The first line contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (1≤n,m≤1⋅103)$$$(1 \le n, m \le 1 \cdot 10^3)$$$ — the number of GPUs and the number of companies.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ (1≤ai≤109)$$$(1 \le a_i \le 10^9)$$$ — the current compute loads of the GPUs.

Each of the following m$$$m$$$ lines describes one company and contains four integers Lj$$$L_j$$$, Rj$$$R_j$$$, Aj$$$A_j$$$, and Bj$$$B_j$$$ (1≤Lj≤Rj≤n,1≤Aj≤Bj≤1012)$$$(1 \le L_j \le R_j \le n,\; 1 \le A_j \le B_j \le 10^{12})$$$, meaning the j$$$j$$$-th company uses all GPUs from index Lj$$$L_j$$$ to Rj$$$R_j$$$ and its total load must lie between Aj$$$A_j$$$ and Bj$$$B_j$$$ inclusive.
output: Print a single integer: the minimal possible k$$$k$$$ such that there exist integer adjustments meeting all company conditions, the per-GPU safety floor ai+Δi≥1$$$a_i + \Delta_i \ge 1$$$, and |Δi|≤k$$$|\Delta_i| \le k$$$ for all GPUs. If no such k$$$k$$$ exists, print −1$$$-1$$$.
note: For the sample test, k=0$$$k = 0$$$ or k=1$$$k = 1$$$ are not feasible. For k=2$$$k = 2$$$, possible final compute load distributions include [4,7,4,6,3]$$$[4, 7, 4, 6, 3]$$$ or [3,8,4,6,2]$$$[3, 8, 4, 6, 2]$$$.
